Implementation Plan Here is the implementation plan for #10120. Exploration confirmed the change belongs in `_evaluate_fp_state`: today a `must_contain` fingerprint whose file is missing is always a violation. Three verifier call sites (the two compare-mode paths and baseline capture) don't pass `captured_at` yet. No open-question blockers remain. # Plan: issue #10120 — fingerprint verifier accepts a base-branch deletion that came after capture Planning ref: `main` @ `d6bae783c44745737eec7735ca3340de2c43832c` (checkout ref `main`; integration-branch mismatch line reads `unknown`, not `true`). The fixed-up content below targets the default branch. `scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py` and `tests/test_conflict_one_sided_delete_workflow_path.py` are identical to `isolated-base` (no diff). Clarification: none needed (the answer was posted automatically). The issue body sets the exact contract and is the spec. ## Automation / wiring (§20.E) - **Script type:** this only changes existing code. No new script, no supervisor, no DB work, and no `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry. - **Wiring:** nothing new. The verifier is already called from: - `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh` (baseline capture and compare during the integration-sync merge, in working-tree mode); - `scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh` (`--list-violated-files`); - `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (wave-dispatch gate, `--ref` mode). - Review runs stage main's copy of the verifier (`.codex-workflow-src-main`). So the fix reaches the wedged `orchestrator/project-9421` sync as soon as it merges. ## Files likely to change - `scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py` - `tests/test_conflict_one_sided_delete_workflow_path.py` - `agents.d/10120-fingerprint-base-deletion-supersede.md` (new) - `changelog.d/10120-fingerprint-base-deletion-supersede.md` (new) ## Acceptance ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_conflict_one_sided_delete_workflow_path.py::test_fingerprint_base_deletion_after_capture_passes red-on-base ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_conflict_one_sided_delete_workflow_path.py::test_fingerprint_base_deletion_after_capture_passes_compare_mode red-on-base ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_conflict_one_sided_delete_workflow_path.py::test_fingerprint_base_deletion_before_capture_still_fails ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_conflict_one_sided_delete_workflow_path.py::test_fingerprint_resolver_deletion_still_fails ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_conflict_one_sided_delete_workflow_path.py::test_fingerprint_base_deletion_supersede_off_switch ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_baseline.py ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_tiers.py ACCEPTANCE: post-merge none: the real proof is the next integration-sync review round on the orchestrator integration branch, not a main-branch workflow. ## Functions or modules to implement All changes are in `scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py`. The model to follow is `_is_must_contain_post_capture_evolution_false_positive` (around lines 532-650). It already has the right shape: zero API calls, local `git log`, fail closed, a module cache, and committer-epoch versus `_captured_at_to_epoch(captured_at)`, plus the `_AI_MERGE_RESOLVE_SUBJECT_PREFIX` check. **1. New constants and module state** (placed next to `_AI_MERGE_RESOLVE_SUBJECT_PREFIX`, line 331): - `_BASE_DELETION_SUPERSEDE_ENV = "INTEGRATION_FINGERPRINT_BASE_DELETION_SUPERSEDE_ENABLED"` - `_BASE_DELETION_SUPERSEDE_CACHE: dict[tuple[str, str, str], tuple[str, str] | None] = {}` - `_BASE_DELETION_SUPERSEDE_FLAG_WARNED: list[bool] = [False]` (one warning per process) - `_SAFE_BASE_BRANCH_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]{0,199}$")`, plus explicit rejects: - `..` - `//` - `@{` - a trailing `/`, `.` or `.lock` A grep found no `base_deletion` / `BASE_DELETION` name anywhere in the repo, so these names don't collide. **2. `_base_deletion_supersede_enabled() -> bool`** - Reads the env var, strips whitespace and lowercases it. - `""` (or unset) or `"true"` → on. - `"false"` → off. - Anything else → off, and prints one warning to stderr (guarded by `_BASE_DELETION_SUPERSEDE_FLAG_WARNED`): `::warning::verify_integration_fingerprints: invalid INTEGRATION_FINGERPRINT_BASE_DELETION_SUPERSEDE_ENABLED=; treating as false (base-deletion supersede off).` - This mirrors the off-switch wording in `scripts/unblock_actions.py` (lines 965-967). **3. `_base_deletion_history_ref(ref) -> tuple[str, str] | None`** returns `(commit_sha, label)`. - **Ref mode** (`_normalize_ref(ref)` not None): - Reject a ref that starts with `-`. - Run `git rev-parse --verify --quiet ^{commit}`. - Label: ``, sanitised. - **Working-tree mode with a merge in progress:** - Run `git rev-parse --verify --quiet MERGE_HEAD^{commit}`. - Label: `MERGE_HEAD`. - **Otherwise:** - Read `BASE_BRANCH` (stripped). If it is empty, or fails `_SAFE_BASE_BRANCH_RE` or the rejects, return None. - If it is non-empty but unsafe, also print a stderr warning with the value sanitised and capped. - Run `git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/remotes/origin/^{commit}`. - Label: `origin/`. - Any non-zero exit, timeout or exception → None (fail closed). - `subprocess.run(..., timeout=GIT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECS)`, as the existing helpers do. **4. `_base_deletion_superseding_commit(ref, captured_at, path) -> tuple[str, str] | None`** returns `(sha, label)`. Steps, in order: 1. If `_base_deletion_supersede_enabled()` is false → None. 2. `captured_epoch = _captured_at_to_epoch(captured_at)`; None → None. 3. `_normalize_repo_path(path)`; error → None. 4. Resolve the history ref (helper 3); None → None. 5. Cache lookup keyed by `(history_sha, normalized_path, str(captured_at).strip())`. 6. Run `git ls-tree --full-tree -z --name-only -- `. Non-zero → None. Any output (the path exists) → None. 7. Run `git log --no-renames --diff-filter=D --max-count=1 --format=%H%x00%ct%x00%s -- `. Non-zero, empty or malformed → None. 8. Accept only if `commit_epoch > captured_epoch` and the subject (after `lstrip()`) does not start with `_AI_MERGE_RESOLVE_SUBJECT_PREFIX`. Return `(sha, label)`; otherwise None. 9. Cache the result. Every exception → None. **5. Hook in `_evaluate_fp_state`**, in the `kind == "must_contain"` and `content is None` branch (around line 1426): - Before it returns the "file does not exist in post-resolve tree" violation, call `_base_deletion_superseding_commit(ref, captured_at, path)`. - On a hit, print to stderr: `::warning::FINGERPRINT_BASE_DELETION_SUPERSEDED_V1 issue=# pr=#
